# USD prim types

hdUE's codeless USD schemas (`resources/generatedSchema.usda`): Xformables whose properties are UE's, with UE's defaults as fallbacks. hdUE's Solaris LOPs author them.

## UnrealLocalFogVolume

A UE Local Fog Volume (ULocalFogVolumeComponent), rendered by hdUE: UE's base volume, a sphere of radius 500 cm, fills the unit sphere of the prim's local space. Realtime only: UE's Path Tracer does not render local fog volumes.

#### Radial Fog Density { #unreal-localfogvolume-radialfogextinction }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:RadialFogExtinction</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeRadialFogExtinction_l4bo</code></dd></div></dl>

The density of the radial fog representing its extinction coefficient at the center of the sphere. The final look of the volume is determined by combining the "Coverage=1-Transmittance" of both radial and height fog in order to achieve both soft edges and height fog.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-lfv-radial-density"></div>

#### Height Fog Density { #unreal-localfogvolume-heightfogextinction }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogExtinction</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeHeightFogExtinction_l4bo</code></dd></div></dl>

The density of the radial fog representing its extinction coefficient at height 0 in the unit sphere. The final look of the volume is determined by combining the "Coverage=1-Transmittance" of both radial and height fog in order to achieve both soft edges and height fog.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-lfv-height-density"></div>

#### Height Fog Falloff { #unreal-localfogvolume-heightfogfalloff }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1000</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>1 to 5000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogFalloff</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeHeightFogFalloff_pzbo</code></dd></div></dl>

Controls how the density decreases as height increases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger. 1.0 is the lowest value before visual artifact are visible at the horizon.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-lfv-height-falloff"></div>

#### Height Fog Offset { #unreal-localfogvolume-heightfogoffset }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>-2 to 2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:HeightFogOffset</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeHeightFogOffset_2xbo</code></dd></div></dl>

Height offset, relative to the actor Z position.

#### Scattering Distribution { #unreal-localfogvolume-fogphaseg }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.2</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 0.999</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:FogPhaseG</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogPhaseG_bobo</code></dd></div></dl>

Controls the phase `G` parameter, describing the directionality of the scattering within this fog volume.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-lfv-phase"></div>

#### Fog Albedo { #unreal-localfogvolume-fogalbedo }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:FogAlbedo</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogAlbedo_bobo</code></dd></div></dl>

Controls the albedo of this fog volume.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-lfv-albedo"></div>

#### Fog Emissive { #unreal-localfogvolume-fogemissive }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0, 0, 0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:FogEmissive</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogEmissive_krbo</code></dd></div></dl>

Controls the emissive color of this fog volume. (Unit = Luminance)

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-lfv-emissive"></div>

#### Start Distance { #unreal-localfogvolume-fogstartdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 10</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:FogStartDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogStartDistance_pzbo</code></dd></div></dl>

Controls the distance after which this volume starts to appear. (Unit = Centimeter) This distance is clamped to be greater than r.LocalFogVolume.GlobalStartDistance.

#### Fog Sort Priority { #unreal-localfogvolume-fogsortpriority }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>-127 to 127</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:localFogVolume:FogSortPriority</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unreallocalFogVolumeFogSortPriority_2xbo</code></dd></div></dl>

The priority can be used as a way to override the sorting by distance. A lower value means the volume will be considered further away, i.e. it will draw behind the one with a higher priority value.

## UnrealPostProcessVolume

A UE Post Process Volume (APostProcessVolume), rendered by hdUE: a box filling the cube from -1 to 1 of the prim's local space (a Cube prim's default extent), whose unreal:postProcess:\<FPostProcessSettings property\> attributes blend into the view by UE's own rules (priority, blend radius and weight, unbound) while the camera is inside or near it. The render settings' unreal:postProcess:\* apply after the volumes, as a camera's do in UE.

#### Priority { #unreal-postprocessvolume-priority }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcessVolume:Priority</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessVolumePriority_krbr</code></dd></div></dl>

Priority of this volume. In the case of overlapping volumes the one with the highest priority overrides the lower priority ones. The order is undefined if two or more overlapping volumes have the same priority.

#### Blend Radius { #unreal-postprocessvolume-blendradius }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>100</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 6000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcessVolume:BlendRadius</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessVolumeBlendRadius_gwbr</code></dd></div></dl>

World space radius around the volume that is used for blending (only if not unbound).

#### Blend Weight { #unreal-postprocessvolume-blendweight }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcessVolume:BlendWeight</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessVolumeBlendWeight_gwbr</code></dd></div></dl>

0:no effect, 1:full effect

#### Enabled { #unreal-postprocessvolume-benabled }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcessVolume:bEnabled</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessVolumebEnabled_krbr</code></dd></div></dl>

Whether this volume is enabled or not.

#### Infinite Extent (Unbound) { #unreal-postprocessvolume-bunbound }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcessVolume:bUnbound</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessVolumebUnbound_krbr</code></dd></div></dl>

Whether this volume covers the whole world, or just the area inside its bounds.

## UnrealExponentialHeightFog

A UE Exponential Height Fog (UExponentialHeightFogComponent), rendered by hdUE: its density is FogDensity at the prim's height (its world position along the up axis). It takes the place of the render settings' unreal:heightFog; UE draws one height fog, the first prim by path.

#### Fog Density { #unreal-heightfog-fogdensity }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.02</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 0.05</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FogDensity</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFogDensity_shbj</code></dd></div></dl>

Global density factor.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-density"></div>

#### Fog Height Falloff { #unreal-heightfog-fogheightfalloff }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.2</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.001 to 2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FogHeightFalloff</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFogHeightFalloff_krbj</code></dd></div></dl>

Height density factor, controls how the density increases as height decreases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-height-falloff"></div>

#### Second Fog Density { #unreal-heightfog-secondfogdata-fogdensity }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 0.05</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogDensity</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogSecondFogDataFogDensity_y2bjn</code></dd></div></dl>

Global density factor for this fog. Density 0 turns the second fog off.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-second-fog-density"></div>

#### Second Fog Height Falloff { #unreal-heightfog-secondfogdata-fogheightfalloff }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.2</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.001 to 2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogHeightFalloff</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogSecondFogDataFogHeightFalloff_qdcjn</code></dd></div></dl>

Height density factor, controls how the density increases as height decreases. Smaller values make the visible transition larger.

#### Second Fog Height Offset { #unreal-heightfog-secondfogdata-fogheightoffset }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:SecondFogData:FogHeightOffset</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogSecondFogDataFogHeightOffset_3bcjn</code></dd></div></dl>

Height offset, relative to the actor position Z.

#### Fog Inscattering Color { #unreal-heightfog-foginscatteringluminance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0, 0, 0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FogInscatteringLuminance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFogInscatteringLuminance_l4bj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Note: when r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored and the volumetric fog Emissive is used instead.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-inscattering-color"></div>

#### Sky Atmosphere Ambient Contribution Color Scale { #unreal-heightfog-skyatmosphereambientcontributioncolorscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:SkyAtmosphereAmbientContributionColorScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogSkyAtmosphereAmbientContributionColorScale_wycj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Color used to modulate the SkyAtmosphere component contribution to the non directional component of the fog. Only effective when r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog\>0

#### Inscattering Color Cubemap { #unreal-heightfog-inscatteringcolorcubemap }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>(empty)</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:InscatteringColorCubemap</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogInscatteringColorCubemap_l4bj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Cubemap that can be specified for fog color, which is useful to make distant, heavily fogged scene elements match the sky. When the cubemap is specified, FogInscatteringColor is ignored and Directional inscattering is disabled. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

#### Sky Light Capture In-Scattering Strength { #unreal-heightfog-skylightcaptureaffectsheightfogstrength }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:SkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogStrength</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogSkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogStrength_0tcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

When \>0 and when r.SupportsSkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogInScattering is true, this will make the sky light capture inject scattered light into the height fog.

#### Sky Light Capture In-Scattering Roughness { #unreal-heightfog-skylightcaptureaffectsheightfogroughness }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.15</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:SkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogRoughness</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogSkyLightCaptureAffectsHeightFogRoughness_nvcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

This is the roughness at which the sky light capture cubemap will be sample to simulate scattering dispersion due to a phase function.

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 360</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:InscatteringColorCubemapAngle</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogInscatteringColorCubemapAngle_qdcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Angle to rotate the InscatteringColorCubemap around the Z axis.

#### Inscattering Texture Tint { #unreal-heightfog-inscatteringtexturetint }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:InscatteringTextureTint</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogInscatteringTextureTint_y2bj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>100000</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>1000 to 1000000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FullyDirectionalInscatteringColorDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFullyDirectionalInscatteringColorDistance_9wcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Distance at which InscatteringColorCubemap should be used directly for the Inscattering Color.

#### Non Directional Inscattering Color Distance { #unreal-heightfog-nondirectionalinscatteringcolordistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1000</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>1000 to 1000000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:NonDirectionalInscatteringColorDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogNonDirectionalInscatteringColorDistance_0tcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Distance at which only the average color of InscatteringColorCubemap should be used as Inscattering Color.

#### Directional Inscattering Exponent { #unreal-heightfog-directionalinscatteringexponent }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>4</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>2 to 64</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringExponent</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringExponent_zgcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Controls the size of the directional inscattering cone, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored and the volumetric fog Scattering Distribution is used instead.

#### Directional Inscattering Start Distance { #unreal-heightfog-directionalinscatteringstartdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>10000</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringStartDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringStartDistance_4ocj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Controls the start distance from the viewer of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - There must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

#### Directional Inscattering Color { #unreal-heightfog-directionalinscatteringluminance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0, 0, 0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringLuminance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringLuminance_micj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Controls the color of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

#### Fog Max Opacity { #unreal-heightfog-fogmaxopacity }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FogMaxOpacity</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFogMaxOpacity_ombj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Maximum opacity of the fog. A value of 1 means the fog can become fully opaque at a distance and replace scene color completely, A value of 0 means the fog color will not be factored in at all.

#### Start Distance { #unreal-heightfog-startdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 5000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:StartDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogStartDistance_ombj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Distance from the camera that the fog will start, in world units.

#### End Distance { #unreal-heightfog-enddistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 500000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:EndDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogEndDistance_fjbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Distance from the camera, on the horizontal XY plane, that the fog will end integrating the lighting and transmittance. Disabled when 0.

#### Fog Cutoff Distance { #unreal-heightfog-fogcutoffdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>100000 to 20000000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FogCutoffDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFogCutoffDistance_6sbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Scene elements past this distance will not have fog applied. This is useful for excluding skyboxes which already have fog baked in.

#### Volumetric Fog { #unreal-heightfog-benablevolumetricfog }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bEnableVolumetricFog</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbEnableVolumetricFog_2xbj</code></dd></div></dl>

Whether to enable Volumetric fog. Scalability settings control the resolution of the fog simulation. Note that Volumetric fog currently does not support StartDistance, FogMaxOpacity and FogCutoffDistance. Volumetric fog also can't match exponential height fog in general as exponential height fog has non-physical behavior.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-volumetric"></div>

#### Scattering Distribution { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogscatteringdistribution }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.2</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>-0.9 to 0.9</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogScatteringDistribution</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogScatteringDistribution_incj</code></dd></div></dl>

Controls the scattering phase function - how much incoming light scatters in various directions. A distribution value of 0 scatters equally in all directions, while .9 scatters predominantly in the light direction. In order to have visible volumetric fog light shafts from the side, the distribution will need to be closer to 0.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-scattering-distribution"></div>

#### Albedo { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogalbedo }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogAlbedo</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogAlbedo_gwbj</code></dd></div></dl>

The height fog particle reflectiveness used by volumetric fog. Water particles in air have an albedo near white, while dust has slightly darker value.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-volumetric-fog-albedo"></div>

#### Emissive { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogemissive }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0, 0, 0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogEmissive</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogEmissive_pzbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Light emitted by height fog. This is a density so more light is emitted the further you are looking through the fog. In most cases skylight is a better choice, however right now volumetric fog does not support precomputed lighting, So stationary skylights are unshadowed and static skylights don't affect volumetric fog at all.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-volumetric-fog-emissive"></div>

#### Extinction Scale { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogextinctionscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.1 to 10</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogExtinctionScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogExtinctionScale_3bcj</code></dd></div></dl>

Scales the height fog particle extinction amount used by volumetric fog. Values larger than 1 cause fog particles everywhere absorb more light.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-extinction-scale"></div>

#### View Distance { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>6000</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>1000 to 10000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogDistance_pzbj</code></dd></div></dl>

Distance over which volumetric fog should be computed, after the start distance. Larger values extend the effect into the distance but expose under-sampling artifacts in details.

#### Start Distance { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogstartdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 5000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogStartDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogStartDistance_u7bj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Distance from the camera that the volumetric fog will start, in world units.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-volumetric-fog-start-distance"></div>

#### Near Fade In Distance { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfognearfadeindistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogNearFadeInDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogNearFadeInDistance_zgcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Distance over which volumetric fog will fade in from the start distance.

#### Static Lighting Scattering Intensity { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogstaticlightingscatteringintensity }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 10</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogStaticLightingScatteringIntensity</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogStaticLightingScatteringIntensity_f5cj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

#### Override Light Colors With Fog Inscattering Colors { #unreal-heightfog-boverridelightcolorswithfoginscatteringcolors }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColors</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColors_s3cj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Whether to use FogInscatteringColor for the Sky Light volumetric scattering color and DirectionalInscatteringColor for the Directional Light scattering color. Make sure your directional light has 'Atmosphere Sun Light' enabled! Enabling this allows Volumetric fog to better match Height fog in the distance, but produces non-physical volumetric lighting that may not match surface lighting.

#### Enable Fog Screen Space Scattering { #unreal-heightfog-benablefsss }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bEnableFSSS</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbEnableFSSS_fjbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Enable FSSS (Fog Screen Space Scattering) to approximate multiple scattering.

#### Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale { #unreal-heightfog-fsssscenecolorscatteringamountscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScale_incj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

The amount of scene color injected into the fog screen space scattering technique. When 0, only the fog luminance will be scattered. When 1, fog and scene luminance will be scattered. When above 1, more scene color can be injected to increase the brightness of the multiple scattering effect, even when the fog is not too intense. We cannot scatter more than the scene color however.

#### Scene Color Scattering Amount Power { #unreal-heightfog-fsssscenecolorscatteringamountpower }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPower</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPower_incj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Apply a power over the amount of scattered scene luminance after it is evaluated using Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale. A value smaller than 1 can show more scattering where the fog is less intense.

#### Spread Scale { #unreal-heightfog-fsssspreadscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FSSSSpreadScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFSSSSpreadScale_xpbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

The scale of the spread for the fog multiple scattering. This basically scales mip level sampled from the blurred screen space FSSS texture. Increasing will make scene and thicker fog look fuzzier. But too high values can cause artifacts such as halos around depth discontinuities.

#### Blur Control { #unreal-heightfog-fsssblurcontrol }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.5</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FSSSBlurControl</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFSSSBlurControl_xpbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

When generating the the blurred screen space FSSS texture, this controls how much of the blurred lower mip levels is injected back into the sharper higher mip levels. A higher value will result in a blurrier result. But when = 1, multiple scattering will be a single average color of the FSSS texture.

#### Holdout { #unreal-heightfog-bholdout }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bHoldout</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbHoldout_jebj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

#### Render In Main Pass { #unreal-heightfog-brenderinmainpass }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bRenderInMainPass</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbRenderInMainPass_6sbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

#### Visible In Reflection Captures { #unreal-heightfog-bvisibleinreflectioncaptures }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bVisibleInReflectionCaptures</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbVisibleInReflectionCaptures_3bcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If true, this component will be visible in reflection captures.

#### Visible In Real Time Sky Captures { #unreal-heightfog-bvisibleinrealtimeskycaptures }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures_qdcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If true, this component will be visible in real-time sky light reflection captures.

## UnrealSkyAtmosphere

A UE Sky Atmosphere (USkyAtmosphereComponent), rendered by hdUE, at the prim's world position (UE's Transform Mode decides whether it is used). It takes the place of the render settings' unreal:skyAtmosphere; UE draws one, the first prim by path.

#### Transform Mode { #unreal-skyatmosphere-transformmode }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>PlanetTopAtAbsoluteWorldOrigin</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:TransformMode</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereTransformMode_6sbn</code></dd></div></dl>

The ground albedo that will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it. Only taken into account when MultiScattering\>0.0.

| Value | Label |
|---|---|
| `ESkyAtmosphereTransformMode::PlanetTopAtAbsoluteWorldOrigin` | PlanetTopAtAbsoluteWorldOrigin |
| `ESkyAtmosphereTransformMode::PlanetTopAtComponentTransform` | PlanetTopAtComponentTransform |
| `ESkyAtmosphereTransformMode::PlanetCenterAtComponentTransform` | PlanetCenterAtComponentTransform |

#### Ground Radius { #unreal-skyatmosphere-bottomradius }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>6360</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.1 to 10000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:BottomRadius</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereBottomRadius_krbn</code></dd></div></dl>

The radius in kilometers from the center of the planet to the ground level.

#### Ground Albedo { #unreal-skyatmosphere-groundalbedo }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.401978, 0.401978, 0.401978</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:GroundAlbedo</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereGroundAlbedo_krbn</code></dd></div></dl>

The ground albedo that will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it. Only taken into account when MultiScattering\>0.0.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-ground-albedo"></div>

#### Atmosphere Height { #unreal-skyatmosphere-atmosphereheight }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>60</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.1 to 200</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:AtmosphereHeight</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereAtmosphereHeight_2xbn</code></dd></div></dl>

The height of the atmosphere layer above the ground in kilometers.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-atmosphere-height"></div>

#### MultiScattering { #unreal-skyatmosphere-multiscatteringfactor }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:MultiScatteringFactor</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereMultiScatteringFactor_75bn</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Factor applied to multiple scattering only (after the sun light has bounced around in the atmosphere at least once). Multiple scattering is evaluated using a dual scattering approach. A value of 2 is recommended to better represent default atmosphere when r.SkyAtmosphere.MultiScatteringLUT.HighQuality=0.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-multiscattering"></div>

#### Trace Sample Count Scale { #unreal-skyatmosphere-tracesamplecountscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.25 to 8</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:TraceSampleCountScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereTraceSampleCountScale_75bn</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Scale the atmosphere tracing sample count. Quality level scalability The sample count is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.SampleCountMax' when 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT' is 0. The sample count is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT.SampleCountMax' when 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT' is 1. The sample count is still clamped for aerial perspective according to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.AerialPerspectiveLUT.SampleCountMaxPerSlice'.

#### Rayleigh Scattering Scale { #unreal-skyatmosphere-rayleighscatteringscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.0331</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighScatteringScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereRayleighScatteringScale_h9bn</code></dd></div></dl>

Rayleigh scattering coefficient scale.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-rayleigh-scale"></div>

#### Rayleigh Scattering { #unreal-skyatmosphere-rayleighscattering }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.1752870090634441, 0.40960725075528703, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighScattering</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereRayleighScattering_c1bn</code></dd></div></dl>

The Rayleigh scattering coefficients resulting from molecules in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer.

#### Rayleigh Exponential Distribution { #unreal-skyatmosphere-rayleighexponentialdistribution }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>8</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.001 to 20</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:RayleighExponentialDistribution</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereRayleighExponentialDistribution_incn</code></dd></div></dl>

The altitude in kilometer at which Rayleigh scattering effect is reduced to 40%.

#### Mie Scattering Scale { #unreal-skyatmosphere-miescatteringscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.003996</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 5</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieScatteringScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieScatteringScale_c1bn</code></dd></div></dl>

Mie scattering coefficient scale.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="sky-mie-scattering"></div>

#### Mie Scattering { #unreal-skyatmosphere-miescattering }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieScattering</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieScattering_6sbn</code></dd></div></dl>

The Mie scattering coefficients resulting from particles in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer. As it becomes higher, light will be scattered more.

#### Mie Absorption Scale { #unreal-skyatmosphere-mieabsorptionscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.000444</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 5</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAbsorptionScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieAbsorptionScale_c1bn</code></dd></div></dl>

Mie absorption coefficient scale.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-mie-absorption-scale"></div>

#### Mie Absorption { #unreal-skyatmosphere-mieabsorption }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAbsorption</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieAbsorption_6sbn</code></dd></div></dl>

The Mie absorption coefficients resulting from particles in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer. As it becomes higher, light will be absorbed more.

#### Mie Anisotropy { #unreal-skyatmosphere-mieanisotropy }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.8</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 0.999</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieAnisotropy</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieAnisotropy_6sbn</code></dd></div></dl>

A value of 0 mean light is uniformly scattered. A value closer to 1 means lights will scatter more forward, resulting in halos around light sources.

#### Mie Exponential Distribution { #unreal-skyatmosphere-mieexponentialdistribution }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1.2</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.001 to 10</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:MieExponentialDistribution</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereMieExponentialDistribution_dfcn</code></dd></div></dl>

The altitude in kilometer at which Mie effects are reduced to 40%.

#### Absorption Scale { #unreal-skyatmosphere-otherabsorptionscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.001881</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 0.2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:OtherAbsorptionScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereOtherAbsorptionScale_l4bn</code></dd></div></dl>

Absorption coefficients for another atmosphere layer. Density increase from 0 to 1 between 10 to 25km and decreases from 1 to 0 between 25 to 40km. This approximates ozone molecules distribution in the Earth atmosphere.

#### Absorption { #unreal-skyatmosphere-otherabsorption }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.34556087187666135, 1, 0.045188729399255716</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:OtherAbsorption</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereOtherAbsorption_gwbn</code></dd></div></dl>

Absorption coefficients for another atmosphere layer. Density increase from 0 to 1 between 10 to 25km and decreases from 1 to 0 between 25 to 40km. The default values represents ozone molecules absorption in the Earth atmosphere.

#### Sky Luminance Factor { #unreal-skyatmosphere-skyluminancefactor }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:SkyLuminanceFactor</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereSkyLuminanceFactor_c1bn</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

#### Aerial Perspective View Distance Scale { #unreal-skyatmosphere-aerialpespectiveviewdistancescale }

#### Height Fog Contribution { #unreal-skyatmosphere-heightfogcontribution }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:HeightFogContribution</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereHeightFogContribution_75bn</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Scale the sky and atmosphere lights contribution to the height fog when SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog project setting is true.

#### Transmittance Min Light Elevation Angle { #unreal-skyatmosphere-transmittanceminlightelevationangle }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>-90</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>-90 to 90</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:TransmittanceMinLightElevationAngle</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereTransmittanceMinLightElevationAngle_0tcn</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

The minimum elevation angle in degree that should be used to evaluate the sun transmittance to the ground. Useful to maintain a visible sun light and shadow on meshes even when the sun has started going below the horizon. This does not affect the aerial perspective.

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.001 to 10</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:AerialPerspectiveStartDepth</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmosphereAerialPerspectiveStartDepth_zgcn</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:skyAtmosphere:bRenderInMainPass</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealskyAtmospherebRenderInMainPass_pzbn</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

## UnrealVolumetricCloud

A UE Volumetric Cloud (UVolumetricCloudComponent), rendered by hdUE with a Sky Atmosphere. It takes the place of the render settings' unreal:volumetricCloud; UE draws one, the first prim by path.

#### Layer Bottom Altitude { #unreal-volumetriccloud-layerbottomaltitude }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>5</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 20</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:LayerBottomAltitude</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudLayerBottomAltitude_75bp</code></dd></div></dl>

The altitude at which the cloud layer starts. (kilometers above the ground)

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-cloud-bottom-altitude"></div>

#### Layer Height { #unreal-volumetriccloud-layerheight }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>10</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.1 to 20</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:LayerHeight</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudLayerHeight_6sbp</code></dd></div></dl>

The height of the the cloud layer. (kilometers above the layer bottom altitude)

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-cloud-layer-height"></div>

#### Tracing Start Max Distance { #unreal-volumetriccloud-tracingstartmaxdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>350</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>1 to 500</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingStartMaxDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudTracingStartMaxDistance_qdcp</code></dd></div></dl>

The maximum distance of the volumetric surface, i.e. cloud layer upper and lower bound, before which we will accept to start tracing. (kilometers)

#### Tracing Start Distance From Camera { #unreal-volumetriccloud-tracingstartdistancefromcamera }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingStartDistanceFromCamera</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudTracingStartDistanceFromCamera_4ocp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

The distance from which the tracing will start. This is useful when the camera for instance is inside the layer of cloud. (kilometers)

#### Tracing Max Distance { #unreal-volumetriccloud-tracingmaxdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>50</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.1 to 500</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:TracingMaxDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudTracingMaxDistance_l4bp</code></dd></div></dl>

The maximum distance that will be traced inside the cloud layer. (kilometers)

#### Planet Radius { #unreal-volumetriccloud-planetradius }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>6360</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.1 to 10000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:PlanetRadius</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudPlanetRadius_tubp</code></dd></div></dl>

The planet radius used when there is not SkyAtmosphere component present in the scene.

#### Ground Albedo { #unreal-volumetriccloud-groundalbedo }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.401978, 0.401978, 0.401978</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:GroundAlbedo</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudGroundAlbedo_tubp</code></dd></div></dl>

The ground albedo used to light the cloud from below with respect to the sun light and sky atmosphere. This is only used by the cloud material when the 'Volumetric Advanced' node have GroundContribution enabled.

#### Material { #unreal-volumetriccloud-material }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>(empty)</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:Material</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudMaterial_bobp</code></dd></div></dl>

The material describing the cloud volume. It must be a Volume domain material. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

#### Use Per Sample Atmospheric Light Transmittance { #unreal-volumetriccloud-busepersampleatmosphericlighttransmittance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:bUsePerSampleAtmosphericLightTransmittance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudbUsePerSampleAtmosphericLightTransmittance_o8cp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Whether to apply atmosphere transmittance per sample, instead of using the light global transmittance.

#### Sky Light Cloud Bottom Occlusion { #unreal-volumetriccloud-skylightcloudbottomocclusion }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.5</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:SkyLightCloudBottomOcclusion</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudSkyLightCloudBottomOcclusion_vlcp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Occlude the sky light contribution at the bottom of the cloud layer. This is a fast approximation to sky lighting being occluded by cloud without having to trace rays or sample AO texture. Ignored if the cloud material explicitely sets the ambient occlusion value.

#### View Sample Count Scale { #unreal-volumetriccloud-viewsamplecountscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.05 to 8</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:ViewSampleCountScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudViewSampleCountScale_u7bp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Scale the tracing sample count in primary views. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.ViewRaySampleCountMax'.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-cloud-view-samples"></div>

#### Reflection View Sample Count Scale Value { #unreal-volumetriccloud-reflectionviewsamplecountscalevalue }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.05 to 8</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:ReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue_9wcp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Scale the tracing sample count in reflection views. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.ReflectionRaySampleMaxCount'.

#### Shadow View Sample Count Scale { #unreal-volumetriccloud-shadowviewsamplecountscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.05 to 8</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowViewSampleCountScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudShadowViewSampleCountScale_micp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Scale the shadow tracing sample count in primary views, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.Shadow.ViewRaySampleMaxCount'.

#### Shadow Reflection View Sample Count Scale Value { #unreal-volumetriccloud-shadowreflectionviewsamplecountscalevalue }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.05 to 8</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudShadowReflectionViewSampleCountScaleValue_16cp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Scale the shadow tracing sample count in reflection views, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows. Quality level scalability CVARs affect the maximum range. The sample count resolution is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.VolumetricCloud.Shadow.ReflectionRaySampleMaxCount'.

#### Shadow Tracing Distance { #unreal-volumetriccloud-shadowtracingdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>15</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.01 to 50</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:ShadowTracingDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudShadowTracingDistance_h9bp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

The shadow tracing distance in kilometers, only used with Advanced Output ray marched shadows.

#### Stop Tracing Transmittance Threshold { #unreal-volumetriccloud-stoptracingtransmittancethreshold }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.005</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:StopTracingTransmittanceThreshold</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudStopTracingTransmittanceThreshold_0tcp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

When the mean transmittance is below this threshold, we stop tracing. This is a good way to reduce the ray marched sample count, and thus to increase performance.

#### Aerial Pespective Rayleigh Scattering Start Distance { #unreal-volumetriccloud-aerialpespectiverayleighscatteringstartdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringStartDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudAerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringStartDistance_thdp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Specify the aerial perspective start distance on cloud for Rayleigh scattering only. (kilometers)

#### Aerial Pespective Rayleigh Scattering Fade Distance { #unreal-volumetriccloud-aerialpespectiverayleighscatteringfadedistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringFadeDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudAerialPespectiveRayleighScatteringFadeDistance_6fdp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Specify the distance over which the Rayleigh scattering will linearly ramp up to full effect. (kilometers)

#### Aerial Pespective Mie Scattering Start Distance { #unreal-volumetriccloud-aerialpespectivemiescatteringstartdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveMieScatteringStartDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudAerialPespectiveMieScatteringStartDistance_o8cp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Specify the aerial perspective start distance on cloud for Mie scattering only. (kilometers)

#### Aerial Pespective Mie Scattering Fade Distance { #unreal-volumetriccloud-aerialpespectivemiescatteringfadedistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:AerialPespectiveMieScatteringFadeDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudAerialPespectiveMieScatteringFadeDistance_16cp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Specify the distance over which the Rayleigh scattering will linearly ramp up to full effect. (kilometers)

#### Holdout { #unreal-volumetriccloud-bholdout }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:bHoldout</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudbHoldout_bobp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

#### Render In Main Pass { #unreal-volumetriccloud-brenderinmainpass }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:bRenderInMainPass</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudbRenderInMainPass_y2bp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

#### Visible In Real Time Sky Captures { #unreal-volumetriccloud-bvisibleinrealtimeskycaptures }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:volumetricCloud:bVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealvolumetricCloudbVisibleInRealTimeSkyCaptures_incp</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If true, this component will be visible in real-time sky light reflection captures.

## UnrealDecal

A UE decal (UDecalComponent), rendered by hdUE: its material projected onto the surfaces inside a box filling the cube from -1 to 1 of the prim's local space, along the prim's local down axis (the stage's up axis, negated). Its material is the bound material (a prepared Substrate Builder decal material), else unreal:decal:DecalMaterial, a cooked path.

#### Decal Material { #unreal-decal-decalmaterial }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>(empty)</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:decal:DecalMaterial</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealdecalDecalMaterial_5fbf</code></dd></div></dl>

Decal material. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

#### Sort Order { #unreal-decal-sortorder }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:decal:SortOrder</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealdecalSortOrder_n8af</code></dd></div></dl>

Controls the order in which decal elements are rendered. Higher values draw later (on top). Setting many different sort orders on many different decals prevents sorting by state and can reduce performance.

#### Fade Screen Size { #unreal-decal-fadescreensize }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.01</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:decal:FadeScreenSize</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealdecalFadeScreenSize_shbf</code></dd></div></dl>

#### Decal Color { #unreal-decal-decalcolor }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:decal:DecalColor</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealdecalDecalColor_99af</code></dd></div></dl>

Decal color, can be accessed using the material Decal Color node.
